newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest air cargo import delays ease to two days.
newsitem.headline: Budapest air cargo import delays ease to two days.

text.p: Budapest's Ferihegy Airport has eased delays over customs clearance of imported cargo to two days from three-four days, airline and airport officials said on Monday.

"Typically, it is now necessary to wait only two days for goods that have arrived to be cleared for delivery to customers," Istvan Horvath, cargo manager for Hungary's airport and air traffic administration LRI, told Reuters.
The delays stem from regulations, effective since September 30, which were designed to improve tracking of cargo movements, Horvath said.
The new rules have resulted in additional paperwork for customs to register goods, thus slowing cargo clearance, he added.
"The customs office added computers and staff at the airport last week to help fulfil the new requirements," he said.

"But this is only part of the solution," Horvath added. "Some delays probably will remain until customs installs the software needed to handle the new regulations properly -- and that might not happen before January."
The delays affect shipments that must be transferred between warehouses of the airport's two cargo handling agents -- LRI and Hungarian national airline Malev Rt, airline industry officials said.
Goods were able to move between the warehouses without paperwork before the new regulations took effect, but customs officials now must register the transferred cargo.
Double registrations occur when one warehouse handles flights with cargo for freight forwarders located at the other warehouse.
Cargo often must be transferred between warehouses because Malev handles most airlines, while most forwarders are based at LRI's facilities, airline and airport officials said.
LRI and Malev compete for each other's business, and they have struggled to work together in adapting to the new rules, officials said.
